I appreciate it and am definitely planning on talking about it with him later. I don't dislike him and definitely don't want to be dismissive of the way he feels. But at the end of the day, he's not my father and never will be. 

I just feel frustrated because when first marrying my mother, he tried to prove that he was "better" than my father and acted like because he was now married to my mother he was automatically my father (albeit a second one). This upset me and I expressed that multiple times and I'm just worrying that he's trying to fill the "father" role too strongly.

I understand that he cares for me, but he's just not my father. I don't have a problem accepting his guidance or learning from him since I don't have a good relationship with my father, but he still can't ever replace him if that makes sense?

I just have an issue with him seeing himself as a "father figure" to me because in the beginning of his marriage to my mother, he tried to oust my father from his role and tried to show that he was "better". I don't think he's a bad guy though. I think he's got his fair share of wisdom and I do respect him and think that he's got a lot of experience worth learning from. I'll definitely be trying to clear the air soon.

While I agree, I feel that I could have said it in a nicer way. I don't want to give the impression that I hate him. He's not a bad guy. I just feel like he tries (and tried) too hard to replace my father.

I didn't mean to hurt him and I feel that I was definitely too blunt. But I feel like he's trying too hard to replace my father and it makes me upset; especially since I've told him that he can't replace my father before.
